name: Cryptic crossword No 27,589
preamble: Four solutions are of a kind, not further defined

clue.text: The occident's fatal day, right?

blocks.note: the Occident is the West, with its possessive S
the Ides of March, the day Caesar was killed
the Tories are the right-wing party in Britain

explanation.surface: A gloomy question about whether the Western world is heading for its day of doom.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble says four answers are of a kind and undefined: they are all musicals. The Ides of March, the date of Caesar's murder, is the classic 'fatal day'.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble's shared kind is stage musicals, and this is Bernstein and Sondheim's 1957 show about rival New York gangs.

clue.text: Thrilled about playing grand that's pulled out

indicators.note: something placed about another goes around it, so one piece encloses the rest

blocks.note: thrilled means elated
a show that is playing is on
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A pianist thrilled about performing on a grand piano that's been wheeled out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand' suggests a piano alongside 'playing', but it is just G, slang for a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pulled out has been stretched, made longer than before.

clue.text: Tango with a modern writer

blocks.note: Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet
W is an abbreviation for with
taken as written
in means fashionable, modern

explanation.surface: A contemporary author dancing the tango.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Modern writer' reads as one phrase, but 'modern' belongs to the wordplay; the writer is far from modern.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain was the pen name of the American author Samuel Clemens.

clue.text: Horn in tune I'd arranged to impress Rattle initially

indicators.note: music that is arranged is reworked into a new form, so these letters get reordered
to impress is to press into, so one piece is pushed inside the other
initially points to the start, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
the first letter of Rattle

explanation.surface: A horn player's tune arranged to impress the conductor Sir Simon Rattle.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word suggests an orchestra: 'Horn' looks like the instrument and Rattle like the conductor Sir Simon Rattle, but 'Horn in' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To horn in is an idiom for butting into something uninvited, which is intruding.

clue.text: Is someone talking about you in this range?

definitions.text: Is someone talking about you in this range?

blocks.note: surface reading: a worry that you are being gossiped about
setter's reading: the distance within which you can hear speech, split into two words it is the burning ears said to signal gossip

explanation.surface: Someone nervously wondering whether people nearby are gossiping about them.
explanation.walkthrough: Folklore says your ears burn when you are being talked about; split as EARS HOT, the answer describes that sign as well as the hearing range.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the distance within which a voice can be heard.

clue.text: Maestro's opera popular in part of UK

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: Tosca is Puccini's opera
NI is Northern Ireland
in means popular

explanation.surface: A conductor's opera production proving a hit in one region of Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is the clue's join: popular sits inside Northern Ireland, after the opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a celebrated Italian conductor, and maestro is the title given to great conductors.

clue.text: It's in chamber music that's sung in parts

blocks.note: first meaning: a cartridge loaded into the chamber of a gun
second meaning: a song where voices enter one after another with the same tune

explanation.walkthrough: 'Chamber music' reads as one phrase, but the split falls between them: the chamber is a gun's.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun cartridge is called this, and so is a canon-style song like Frère Jacques sung by staggered voices.

clue.text: Initiate men in order

blocks.note: to blood someone is to initiate them, originally a young hunter
members of a religious order are brothers

explanation.surface: Welcoming new members into a brotherhood.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the preamble's four undefined musicals. 'Blood' as a verb means to give someone their first experience of something.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the preamble's stage musicals: Willy Russell's long-running show about twins separated at birth in Liverpool.

clue.text: A chef explains cooking

indicators.note: cooking mixes and transforms ingredients, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, all thirteen letters

explanation.surface: A cook talks you through a recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: Another of the four undefined musicals. A sixpence was a small pre-decimal British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the preamble's stage musicals, the 1963 show starring Tommy Steele, based on H. G. Wells's novel Kipps.

clue.text: John escorts royal couple circling behind nurse

indicators.note: to circle something is to go right round it, so a pair surrounds the next piece

blocks.note: john is slang for a toilet
K for king and ER for queen
aft means at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A man named John guards the king and queen while a nurse follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a courtier but is the toilet; ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the Queen, so the royal couple splits as K and ER.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse a patient is to tend and care for them.

clue.text: Rookie wearing militia's diving gear

indicators.note: someone wearing clothes is inside them, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: the SA was the Nazi Brownshirt militia
a cub is a beginner, as in cub reporter

explanation.surface: A new recruit kitted out in the paramilitary's diving equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's sits between wordplay and definition as a join.
explanation.definitionFit: The acronym stands for self-contained underwater breathing apparatus, the kit worn by divers.

clue.text: Buccaneer, heading off, stops here

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the instrument where stops are found

indicators.note: with its head gone, a word loses its first letter

blocks.note: Henry Morgan was a famous Welsh buccaneer

explanation.surface: A pirate sets sail and calls at this port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stops' looks like a verb about the pirate halting; it is the noun for the knobs on an organ that select sets of pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pipe organs have stops, the drawknobs a player pulls to bring different ranks of pipes into use.

clue.text: Exceptional catch found swimming around

indicators.note: things swimming move about freely, so the letters drift into a new order
going around something encloses it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
to catch what someone says is to hear it

explanation.surface: An angler's remarkable catch, spotted swimming about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch' wants to be a fish; here it means to hear something said.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without precedent, never before reported, is exceptional.

clue.text: Cotton? It beats worsted

indicators.note: worsted means beaten or defeated, and beaten things are knocked out of shape

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A boast that cotton cloth is better than worsted wool.
explanation.walkthrough: Worsted is a wool fabric, so it sits naturally beside cotton; here it is the old verb meaning defeated.
explanation.definitionFit: Batiste is a fine, lightweight woven fabric, usually made of cotton or linen.

clue.text: Pantry in big house, ideal place to hear music

blocks.note: first meaning: a storeroom in a country house for preserves and drinks, once used for distilling
second meaning: a quiet room with no noise, read as two plain words

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a real historical term from English country houses; the second just reads the two words literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand houses kept a storeroom for cordials and preserves, and a quiet chamber is best for listening.

clue.text: Hears about extremely old valves

indicators.note: lying about something means surrounding it, so one piece encloses the other
the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outer letters stay

blocks.note: a judge hears a case, that is, tries it
the first and last letters of old

explanation.surface: Someone listening to talk about antique radio valves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hears' means tries in the legal sense, a court hearing a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A triode is a thermionic valve with three electrodes, the vacuum tube of early radios.

clue.text: Dance music on river drowns small talk

indicators.note: something drowned is submerged inside water, so one piece goes under and within another

blocks.note: disco is a style of dance music
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Loud music on a riverboat party drowns out the small talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small talk' is a phrase the solver reads as one unit, but 'small' is S for the wordplay and 'talk' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A discourse is a formal spoken or written treatment of a subject, essentially talk.

clue.text: American folk playing short melody with it

indicators.note: something short is cut down, so the last letter is dropped
playing with things moves them about, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the word lacking its final letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: American folk musicians playing a brief tune along with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two parts of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-time is a genre of traditional American country music, fiddle and banjo led, so a type of folk.

clue.text: Train voice

blocks.note: first meaning: a fast train making few stops
second meaning: to put a feeling or thought into words

explanation.walkthrough: 'Train voice' suggests training a singer, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a fast rail service and a verb for stating opinions aloud in words.

clue.text: Fine tunes coming from women

definitions.note: the answer is a collective noun phrase for women

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
airs are tunes
ex is Latin for from, as in ex works

explanation.surface: Lovely songs sung by a women's choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like an adjective for the tunes but is F, and 'from' supplies EX.
explanation.definitionFit: The fair sex is an old-fashioned and now dated collective phrase for women.

clue.text: More strong doubt about concert opening in Queens

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the word runs backwards
an opening is the very start, so just the first letter is wanted
being in something means sitting inside it, so one letter is enclosed

blocks.note: an if is a doubt, as in ifs and buts
ER is the Queen, so two queens give ER twice
the first letter of concert

explanation.surface: Growing uncertainty about a concert premiere in New York's borough of Queens.
explanation.walkthrough: Queens looks like the New York borough; it is ER (Elizabeth Regina) twice, with the C between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiercer is the comparative of fierce, meaning more intense, violent or powerful.

clue.text: What to eat in a basement together?

definitions.text: What to eat in a basement together?

blocks.clueFragment: What to eat in a basement
blocks.note: surface reading: food for a meal down in the cellar
setter's reading: run 'a basement' together into one word, abasement, and ask what is eaten when humiliated

explanation.surface: Planning a shared supper in the cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Together' tells you to close the gap in 'a basement', giving abasement, the state of humiliation in which one proverbially eats this dish.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat it is the idiom for apologising humbly and accepting humiliation after being proved wrong.

clue.text: Place for minister's son in Hair

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one letter is enclosed

blocks.note: a mane is a head of hair
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A role for a clergyman's son in the musical Hair.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital H makes 'Hair' look like the 1960s musical, apt in a puzzle themed on musicals; it is just a mane.
explanation.definitionFit: A manse is the house provided for a minister, especially in the Scottish Presbyterian church.

clue.text: Finished wrapping rare part of bagpipes

indicators.note: wrapping something covers it all round, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: finished means done
R is an abbreviation for rare

explanation.surface: Someone has wrapped up an unusual bit of a bagpipe set.
explanation.walkthrough: R for rare is a standard abbreviation, as on a steak menu; it goes inside the word for finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagpipes have drones, the pipes that sound one continuous bass note beneath the melody.

clue.text: Star turns up during the Benedicite

indicators.note: during means within the span of something, so the letters lie inside the phrase
in a down clue, turning up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: letters spanning the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A celebrity singer shows up in the middle of a church canticle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Benedicite is a canticle in which all creation, stars included, praises God, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Deneb is the brightest star in the constellation Cygnus, the swan.

clue.text: Royal bash involves performing music

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap in, so one piece takes another inside

blocks.note: R is short for royal, as in RN
a performer on stage is on
a bash is a party, a do

explanation.surface: A royal party with live musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involves' applies to the whole royal bash, so the performing piece slips between its two parts; bash and do are both British slang for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical form in which a main theme keeps returning between contrasting episodes.

clue.text: Odd way of talking doesn't begin in Morecambe

indicators.note: failing to begin means the opening letter is lost
being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: Eric Morecambe, the British comedian of Morecambe and Wise
an accent is a way of speaking

explanation.surface: A strange local accent is fading out in the seaside town of Morecambe.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe is a Lancashire resort, but here it stands for the comedian Eric Morecambe, so it gives his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric person or habit is unconventional, peculiar and strange.

clue.text: British in Marseilles defaced art there

indicators.note: something defaced has been spoiled and disfigured, so these letters are knocked into a new shape

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
taken as written
in French, spoken in Marseilles, thou art is tu es

explanation.surface: A British vandal in Marseilles spoilt the artwork there.
explanation.walkthrough: The last of the four undefined musicals. 'There' places 'art' in France, where the archaic 'thou art' is 'tu es'.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the preamble's stage musicals, adapted from Victor Hugo's novel and staged in London since 1985.
